answer: Rotating Resource Quota. Each identity must submit a fresh, signed work receipt showing it converted a unique physical input (a logged timber batch, a tagged pearl lot, a glacier melt sample) into a registered output within the last epoch. The ledger rejects any receipt whose input hash already appears, so one physical batch cannot back two identities. An attacker must acquire and process new genuine inputs per identity per epoch, paying sourcing, transport, and verification costs repeatedly.
